drug_class: Vitamin D analog (synthetic form of Vitamin D)
purpose: Doxercalciferol is used to lower high levels of a hormone called parathyroid hormone (PTH) in people with chronic kidney disease, including those on dialysis. High PTH can weaken your bones and cause other serious health problems. This medication helps keep your bones and minerals like calcium and phosphorus at healthier levels.
how_it_works: Your kidneys normally help activate Vitamin D in your body, but when your kidneys are not working well, they cannot do this job properly. Doxercalciferol is a man-made form of Vitamin D that your body can activate even when your kidneys are struggling. Once activated, it tells your parathyroid glands to slow down and make less PTH, which helps protect your bones and overall health.
common_side_effects: Feeling tired or weak, headache, dizziness, nausea, vomiting, swelling in your hands or feet, and dry mouth. You may also notice changes in your appetite or have constipation.
warnings: This medication can raise your calcium and phosphorus levels too high, which can be dangerous and cause serious heart, kidney, or blood vessel problems. Tell your doctor right away if you feel very thirsty, urinate a lot, have muscle weakness, confusion, or irregular heartbeat. Avoid taking extra Vitamin D supplements unless your doctor tells you to. Regular blood tests are very important to make sure your levels stay safe.
typical_dosing: The dose is adjusted based on your PTH, calcium, and phosphorus blood levels. For dialysis patients, a typical starting dose is about 10 micrograms given three times per week during dialysis, either by injection or by mouth as a capsule. Your doctor will adjust your dose based on your lab results, so it is important to keep all your appointments and blood tests.
